$schema_note: Native API inventory for embedding: Aether C API (Rust, JSON-over-C-ABI, job-polled) and Zeptun C ABI + JNI (Zig, error-code style).

aether.header: no header in this repository; the docs reference ios/Shared/aether.h in the (separate) Oblivion client project; functions declared via #[no_mangle] pub extern "C" in aether/src/ffi.rs
aether.style: handle-based, polled (no callbacks into the host); every call returns a *mut c_char JSON string that the caller frees with aether_string_free; panics are caught at the boundary; async work runs on an internal tokio runtime as jobs

functions.name: aether_version
functions.purpose: {"ok":true,"version":"2.4.0"}

functions.name: aether_string_free
functions.purpose: free a returned JSON string; null-safe

functions.name: aether_job_poll
functions.purpose: poll a job: {state:running} or {state:done, result:{...}}

functions.name: aether_job_cancel
functions.purpose: cancel a job

functions.name: aether_job_free
functions.purpose: drop a finished/running job (cancels it)

functions.name: aether_identity_open
functions.purpose: open or provision an identity: {path, transport?, model?, locale?, team?{team,client_id,client_secret,token,email}} -> job -> {identity:id, summary, path, lastconn_path}

functions.name: aether_identity_summary
functions.purpose: device/ipv4/ipv6/organization summary

functions.name: aether_identity_free
functions.purpose: drop an identity handle

functions.name: aether_scan_start
functions.purpose: scan for an endpoint: {transport?, mode?, ip?, profile?, ports?, excluded?, ech?} -> job -> {endpoint:{addr,rtt_ms}}

functions.name: aether_verify_start
functions.purpose: verify an endpoint before connecting: {peer, transport?, socks?, http?, profile?, keepalive?, ech?} -> job -> {reachable:bool}

functions.name: aether_tunnel_start
functions.purpose: connect the tunnel and serve SOCKS5 (and optional HTTP) until it closes or is cancelled: same payload as verify -> job -> {state:closed|stopped}
functions.notes: Reconnect behavior: this is the api::connect path; the full CLI core (run_with) additionally loops across tunnels. The tunnel job ending does NOT necessarily mean the process should exit - poll and restart as needed. NOTE: api::connect sets AETHER_HTTP_PROXY via env (api.rs L558) - process-global.

functions.name: aether_core_start
functions.purpose: run the WHOLE CLI core in-process with the given argument vector (same parser as the binary); null/empty = no args (interactive questions would read stdin - always pass args)
functions.notes: CAUTION: the CLI parser mutates process environment variables (std::env::set_var) - one core instance per process; do not run two cores or a core plus other env-sensitive code concurrently.

functions.name: aether_team_sign_in
functions.purpose: Zero Trust interactive sign-in -> {token}

functions.name: aether_team_code_request
functions.purpose: request an email login code -> {session:id,email}

functions.name: aether_team_code_resend
functions.purpose: resend the code

functions.name: aether_team_code_submit
functions.purpose: submit the code -> {signed_in, token?}

functions.name: aether_team_session_free
functions.purpose: drop a sign-in session

functions.name: aether_team_token_set
functions.purpose: store a Zero Trust token

functions.name: aether_team_token_clear
functions.purpose: forget the token

caveats: No official C header in this repository - generate one from ffi.rs declarations (cbindgen or hand-written) or reuse the Oblivion client's ios/Shared/aether.h.
Job-based: results are polled; no blocking wait and no host callbacks.

The fine-grained API (identity/scan/verify/tunnel) does NOT expose every CLI option; aether_core_start with an argument vector covers the full surface (at the cost of env-var mutation and single-instance limits).
The data path is channel-based with no TUN code (DOCS.en.md 'Using Aether as a library').

std::env::set_var in a multi-threaded process is thread-unsafe by Rust semantics (UB risk in strict builds); Aether itself calls it extensively - embed, don't run concurrent cores, and keep the host single-threaded around core start.
prior_art: PattNG (https://github.com/patterniha/PattNG) - Android app running Aether with a tun front end (referenced by Docs/OPENWRT.en.md)
An iOS client ('Oblivion', header ios/Shared/aether.h) is referenced by DOCS.en.md as the consumer of this C API

zeptun.library: libzeptun.a + shared library (zig build) / libzeptun.so (Android) / Zeptun.xcframework (Apple)
zeptun.header: include/zeptun.h (hand-written, stable; integer error codes, fixed-size structs with struct_size + reserved fields, no Zig types)

functions.name: zeptun_version / zeptun_version_string
functions.purpose: ABI version / human version

functions.name: zeptun_strerror
functions.purpose: error code -> message

functions.name: zeptun_config_init
functions.purpose: fill config struct with preset defaults (struct_size must be set)

functions.name: zeptun_create
functions.purpose: create an engine (validates config)

functions.name: zeptun_create_from_json / zeptun_create_from_toml
functions.purpose: create from a JSON/TOML document (unknown keys rejected)

functions.name: zeptun_destroy
functions.purpose: join workers, remove routes, free everything; once; never from a callback; never concurrent
functions.evidence: zeptun.h L196; wiki C-API thread table

functions.name: zeptun_set_log_callback
functions.purpose: process-wide log sink (message NOT NUL-terminated); call before creating engines

functions.name: zeptun_set_read_callback
functions.purpose: packets leaving the engine, batches up to 128 (EXTERNAL mode)

functions.name: zeptun_set_passthrough_callback
functions.purpose: packets for passthrough handler

functions.name: zeptun_set_protect_callback
functions.purpose: called with every upstream socket fd before it connects; return false to fail the connection (Android VpnService.protect)

functions.name: zeptun_set_flow_callback
functions.purpose: per-flow verdict: PROXY | DIRECT | DROP | REJECT (TCP reset / ICMP unreachable); ZeptunFlow = {protocol 6|17, family 4|6, src, dst, sport, dport}
functions.notes: THE cross-platform loop-prevention hook: return DIRECT for Aether's WARP endpoint/API destinations so they are dialed outside the tunnel on every OS.

functions.name: zeptun_set_device_fd
functions.purpose: adopt a TUN descriptor (VpnService / NEPacketTunnelProvider)

functions.name: zeptun_set_adapter_guid
functions.purpose: pin the Wintun adapter GUID (used only at creation)

functions.name: zeptun_start
functions.purpose: spawn workers; with a TUN device returns once every queue is ready and routes are installed

functions.name: zeptun_run
functions.purpose: run ONE worker on the calling thread until zeptun_stop (host owns threads; libc-free Android lib requires this)

functions.name: zeptun_stop
functions.purpose: stop from any thread, including from a callback; returns immediately

functions.name: zeptun_write_packet / zeptun_write_packets
functions.purpose: inject packets into the engine (EXTERNAL mode)
functions.thread_safety: any number of threads; WOULD_BLOCK/short count on full queue

functions.name: zeptun_inject_packets
functions.purpose: inject packets that skip the stack (passthrough)

functions.name: zeptun_network_changed
functions.purpose: tell the engine the default route moved (rebinds upstreams, drops cached proxy connections, refreshes routes)

functions.name: zeptun_stats
functions.purpose: lock-free counter snapshot (version 3; 35 counters incl. socks5_pool_hits, dns_fake_answers, tcp/udp_migrated)

functions.name: zeptun_memory
functions.purpose: packet pool usage: buffers, in_use, resident_bytes, released_bytes, starved_flows, exhausted

functions.name: zeptun_interface_name
functions.purpose: name of the created interface

structs.ZeptunConfig: struct_size + preset + device_kind(TUN/FD/EXTERNAL) + tun_fd + tun_name[16] + mtu + queues + offload + configure + address4[64] + address6[64] + stack_mode + handler_kind + socks5_server[64]/username[256]/password[256]/udp/pipeline + auto_route + passthrough_gso + fwmark + route_table + rule_priority + io_backend + max/tcp/udp sessions + tcp_rx_window/tx_buffer + udp/tcp idle timeouts + memory_budget + log_level + workers + reserved[8]
structs.ZeptunFlow: protocol (6|17), family (4|6), source[16], destination[16], source_port, destination_port
structs.ZeptunStats: version, workers, rx/tx packets+bytes, drops, parse_errors, pool_exhausted, gso/gro counters, tcp_* lifecycle, udp_*, icmp_*, nat_active, handoffs, upstream bytes, fragments_reassembled, timeouts, socks5_pool_*, dns_*
structs.ZeptunMemory: version, workers, buffers, in_use, resident_bytes, released_bytes, starved_flows, exhausted

jni_bridge.library: libzeptun-jni.so (built by ndk-build from src/jni/zeptun_jni.c; class dev/zeptun/Zeptun, override ZEPTUN_JNI_CLASS at compile time)
methods: nativeStart(service: Any?, fd: Int, config: String?): Int - creates engine from TOML (or mobile preset), adopts fd, installs protect callback (calls VpnService.protect(int) via global ref), runs zeptun_run on a pthread
nativeStop(): Unit - zeptun_stop + pthread_join + zeptun_destroy + release global ref
nativeCounter(index: Int): Long - raw field index into ZeptunStats after version/workers (fragile across versions; prefer stats struct via C API)
jni_bridge.constraints: ONE engine per process (static context); no per-instance handles exposed to Java

zeptun.thread_safety_table: version/strerror/config_init pure; set_log_callback process-wide before engines; create any thread; all other setters before start/run else ALREADY_RUNNING; write/inject any threads (WOULD_BLOCK); stats/memory/stop any thread incl. callbacks; destroy once, never from callback; callbacks run on worker threads and must not block
zeptun.linking: Linux libs link libc (worker threads in any C host); Android library is libc-free unless -Dandroid-libc (then call zeptun_run on your own thread - the JNI bridge does exactly this with pthread_create)

embedding_summary.aether: Link libaether (staticlib/cdylib). Recommended entry: aether_core_start with a JSON array of CLI arguments for full option coverage, OR the fine-grained identity->scan->verify->tunnel flow for a managed UI. Poll jobs; free strings; one core per process (env-var mutation).
embedding_summary.zeptun: Link libzeptun (static or shared; xcframework on Apple). zeptun_config_init(preset) or create_from_toml/json, set device fd (VpnService/NE) or EXTERNAL callbacks, set protect + flow + log callbacks before start, then zeptun_start (spawns workers) or zeptun_run (own thread). zeptun_stats/memory for live counters; zeptun_stop + destroy for teardown; routes removed on destroy even after crash.
